proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local argument, not source text. Fix x, g=grad f(x), H=Hess f(x), q(s)=g^T s+s^T Hs/2+L||s||^3/6. Since L>0, q is continuous and coercive, hence attains a global minimum. For any global minimizer s, write r=||s||. Differentiability, including at s=0, gives g+Hs+(L/2)rs=0. Comparing q(s)<=q(-s) gives g^T s<=0. Taking the inner product of stationarity with s gives s^T Hs=-g^T s-(L/2)r^3, so q(s)=g^T s/2-Lr^3/12<=-Lr^3/12. Hessian Lipschitz continuity yields R_g=grad f(x+s)-g-Hs=int_0^1[Hess f(x+ts)-H]s dt, so ||R_g||<=Lr^2/2. Applying that bound to ts and integrating the scalar gradient identity yields |f(x+s)-f(x)-g^T s-s^T Hs/2|<=int_0^1 (L/2)t^2 r^3 dt=Lr^3/6. Therefore f(x+s)<=f(x)+q(s) and f(x)-f(x+s)>=Lr^3/12. Also ||grad f(x+s)||<=||g+Hs||+||R_g||<=Lr^2. These identities include r=0 without division. Thus ||grad f(x{i+1})||^(3/2)<=L^(3/2)ri^3<=12 sqrt(L)[f(xi)-f(x{i+1})]. Summing i=0,...,k-1 telescopes and uses f(xk)>=f_low to give the stated sum bound. The minimum of k nonnegative gradient norms raised to power 3/2 is at most their average. Raising to power 2/3 gives the minimum bound; substituting the stated integer budget gives the epsilon claim, also for Delta=0. This proof does not need Proposition 1, Theorem 10 or any external ARC lead.

assumptions: f:R^d->R is C^2 and ||Hess f(x)-Hess f(y)||<=L||x-y|| for every x,y in R^d.
f(x)>=f_low for all x, where f_low is a finite real number.
L is known; derivatives and global cubic subproblem solves are exact.
statement.conclusion: For all i>=0, f(xi)-f(x{i+1})>=L ri^3/12 and ||grad f(x{i+1})||<=L ri^2. Thus sum_{j=1}^k ||grad f(xj)||^(3/2)<=12 sqrt(L)Delta and min_{1<=j<=k}||grad f(xj)||<=(12 sqrt(L)Delta/k)^(2/3). Any integer k>=1 with k>=12 sqrt(L)Delta/epsilon^(3/2) ensures epsilon-stationarity among these iterates; max(1,ceil(12 sqrt(L)Delta/epsilon^(3/2))) suffices, including Delta=0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use Euclidean vector and spectral matrix norms. Let m_x(s)=f(x)+grad f(x)^T s+s^T Hess f(x)s/2+L||s||^3/6. Starting at x0, choose any global minimizer si of m_{xi} over R^d and set x{i+1}=xi+si; ri=||si|| and Delta=f(x0)-f_low.
statement.parameter_domains: Integer d>=1; real L>0; finite Delta>=0; integer k>=1; real epsilon>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible f, every x0, every choice of global minimizers, every i>=0 and every integer k>=1. Deterministic; uniqueness is unnecessary.
